subject: Money
title: Crypto and Taxes
description: A short lesson to help you apply Crypto and Taxes.

hook.text: In 2021, the IRS added a question to every tax return: 'Did you sell any digital assets this year?'

buildup.text: Crypto is treated as property, not currency. Every trade, swap, and even spending triggers a taxable event.

discovery.text: Buy Bitcoin at $10,000, sell at $50,000: you owe capital gains tax on the $40,000 profit.

twist.text: Early crypto users treated it as invisible to tax authorities. The IRS now tracks blockchain transactions.

climax.text: Decentralized finance meets centralized taxation. The tension is unresolved and growing.

punchline.text: The blockchain never forgets. Neither does the IRS.

quiz.question: How does the IRS classify cryptocurrency?
